articles.title: I Automated Python Docstrings for a Month — The Workflow That Finally Stuck
articles.excerpt: Here is a confession most Python developers recognise: I have never kept docstrings current by willpower alone. Not once, across a full project. The deadline lands, the function works, and the docstri…
articles.body: Here is a confession most Python developers recognise: I have never kept docstrings current by willpower alone. Not once, across a full project. The deadline lands, the function works, and the docstring becomes "one line for now" — then two months later it describes the previous signature, which is worse than no docstring at all, because readers trust it. So last month I stopped writing docstrings by hand entirely and ran two very different things in their place: a ~40-line stdlib audit script, and dedicated AI doc tools. Then I had a separate AI model grade the output blind. This is what survived, what broke, and the loop I still have running today. What the standard library gives you for free Before paying anyone anything, know how far the stdlib gets you.

articles.title: Export Large Data With Chunk in Laravel-Excel: Fix
articles.excerpt: The most common mistake developers make when exporting thousands of database records is loading every row into memory before generating the Excel file. Calling Model::all() or Model::get() inside an e…
articles.body: The most common mistake developers make when exporting thousands of database records is loading every row into memory before generating the Excel file. Calling Model::all() or Model::get() inside an export may work perfectly during development, then fail when the production database grows. If you need to export large data with chunk in laravel-excel , the fix is usually to stop building a full collection and let Laravel Excel retrieve database records in smaller batches. Quick answer: Use Laravel Excel's FromQuery concern instead of FromCollection with Model::all() or Model::get() . Return an Eloquent query without executing it. Laravel Excel processes the query in chunks automatically.

articles.title: Your coding agent shouldn't grade its own homework
articles.excerpt: Scrolling X today, the same idea kept showing up in different repos: add a review step before agent code gets pushed, and don't let the agent that wrote the code decide it's done. I agree, and it's th…
articles.body: Scrolling X today, the same idea kept showing up in different repos: add a review step before agent code gets pushed, and don't let the agent that wrote the code decide it's done. I agree, and it's the rule I ended up building around. Why self-review doesn't work When one model writes the code and then checks it, it tends to repeat its own blind spots. The assumptions that produced the bug are the same ones it uses to review it. Rerunning the same model with "please double-check" mostly gets you more confidence, not more coverage. What helped in practice Run deterministic checks first. Linters, tests, secret scanners. They catch the boring stuff cheaply, so any model review can spend its attention on intent and edge cases. Use a different model as the reviewer.

articles.title: Why Legacy Wingdings Fonts Break on Mobile & How to Map Them to Unicode
articles.excerpt: If you have ever attempted to render classic dingbat symbols—like those from Microsoft's iconic Wingdings (1, 2, 3) or Webdings font families—on a modern web page or mobile device, you have likely run…
articles.body: If you have ever attempted to render classic dingbat symbols—like those from Microsoft's iconic Wingdings (1, 2, 3) or Webdings font families—on a modern web page or mobile device, you have likely run into an annoying problem: instead of visual icons, users see ordinary Latin characters like A , B , or J . In this short deep-dive, let's explore why this happens and how modern Unicode mapping provides a clean, zero-dependency solution. 1. The Historical Root Cause: ASCII Remapping Back in the early 1990s (Windows 3.1 era), standard character encodings were largely 8-bit, and the Unicode consortium was still in its infancy. Microsoft created Wingdings by taking a standard TrueType font and replacing the visual glyphs of standard ASCII byte values (0x20 through 0x7E) with custom icons.

articles.body: By the time Grand Theft Auto 4 launched in 2008, Rockstar had carved itself an unassailable niche and a reputation for innovation. And yet for all that praise, it was pretty easy to guess what a new GTA game would be like. The formula changed little from the time the series went 3D. Some vaguely sympathetic character would encounter hardship and then embrace a life of crime as a little treat. That life might look different from game to game, but the general idea remained the same. GTA 4 defied that pattern, and it's one of the reasons it's still an excellent game.

articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

While a chatbot mostly gives you answers or helps you figure out how to do something, an AI agent can actually perform those tasks for you. articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
articles.author: Dan Goodin

articles.title: When not to watch a meteor shower — why I'm not staying up for the Orionids
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week, but a bright moon makes much of the night less than ideal. Sometimes the sensible observing decision is knowing when to stay in bed — and when to get up earl…
articles.body: I used to think being interested in the night sky meant I had to try every meteor shower. If a calendar said "peak," I interpreted that as an instruction. I'd set an alarm, find several layers of clothing and go outside at around 2:00 a.m. when even the neighborhood cats seemed surprised to see me. Then I'd spend an increasingly resentful 45 minutes staring upward, occasionally see one meteor and wonder whether I was somehow doing it all wrong. As I've grown into stargazing, I've become much more selective. The Orionids peak next week, and normally I'd be tempted. These fast meteors come from debris from Halley's Comet , which is enough of a connection to make almost anyone want to go outside.

articles.title: Scientists find 'gemstones' in atmosphere of bizarre, scorching-hot 'marshmallow' exoplanet
articles.excerpt: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have unravelled some of the secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot exoplanet that has the consistency of marshmallow.
articles.body: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST , is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this " hot Jupiter " skyrocket.

articles.title: Researchers Demonstrate OpenBSD Root Exploit Chaining 37-Year-Old Shared-Memory Bug
articles.excerpt: A local privilege escalation exploit published today gains root on OpenBSD 7.9 by chaining a roughly 37-year-old integer overflow with a separate kernel flaw, bypassing OpenBSD's KARL kernel-address r…
articles.body: A local privilege escalation exploit published today gains root on OpenBSD 7.9 by chaining a roughly 37-year-old integer overflow with a separate kernel flaw, bypassing OpenBSD's KARL kernel-address randomization and its SMAP and SMEP hardware protections. Security firm Calif, which found and reported the flaws, published a detailed writeup and full proof-of-concept code after OpenBSD shipped
